name: Forlorn Cloister
summary: Among the tombs of Forlorn Cloister, the fallen dead rise, and Scarlet Crusaders burn their bodies to stop them.

sections.title: A Consecration Consumed
sections.body:
You enter a graveyard where Scarlet Crusaders hurry between tombs with torches. They burn their fallen brothers, but the plague has already tainted the earth beneath them.

Once, priests and paladins of Lordaeron laid their honoured dead here in peace. Now spectres drift between the crypts, and corpses claw their way from the graves. The Crusaders keep watch, yet dark magic deep in the grounds still calls the dead to rise.

sections.title: The Master of the Tombs
sections.body: Bloodmage Thalnos commands the dead within the cloister. A skeletal sorcerer, he is another of the Monastery's tragedies, lost to undeath and hungry for vengeance. With dark magic, he binds the souls of the deceased and slaughters anyone who enters his blighted graveyard.

faq.q: Where is the Forlorn Cloister located?
faq.answer: Forlorn Cloister occupies the outdoor graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery, in the northeastern corner of Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: Why are the Scarlet Crusaders burning bodies here?
faq.answer: The Scarlet Crusade burns its fallen in a desperate effort to keep the Scourge plague from raising them. The cloister's soil is already tainted, and unburned bodies soon rise as mindless zombies.

faq.q: Who rules over the Forlorn Cloister?
faq.answer: Bloodmage Thalnos rules the graveyard. The powerful undead spellcaster commands the wandering dead and attacks living intruders.

faq.q: Why is the graveyard haunted if the Scarlet Crusade holds the Monastery?
faq.answer: The Scarlet Crusaders have lost control of their cemetery despite their religious fervour. Necromantic energies sweeping through Lordaeron have stirred the buried dead, leaving the living garrison in a ceaseless fight against the spirits of their former peers.

angles.text: As a priest, you see what happens when a holy sanctum falls to darkness. Sacred rites give way to frantic pyres, and tortured apparitions roam the grounds.
As Forsaken, you may see a grim irony here. The zealous Crusaders brand all undead as monsters, yet cannot stop their own brothers from rising beneath their feet.
